blogs.title: When the Neck Swells Without Wheeze: Dermatomyositis Masquerading as Angioedema
blogs.description: Explore the classic 'red herring' where dermatomyositis presents as isolated neck edema, mimicking deep neck space infections or idiopathic angioedema. This post analyzes the pitfalls of assuming a histaminergic or bradykinin mechanism without checking for non-histaminergic causes, emphasizing why CK levels and a search for subtle cutaneous clues (like nailfold changes) are critical first steps in unexplained neck swelling.

blogs.title: The Anti-SAE1 Phenotype: When Dysphagia Precedes the Rash
blogs.description: Dive into the specific clinical profile of Anti-SAE1 antibody-positive dermatomyositis. Unlike classic presentations driven by TIF1-γ (malignancy risk) or Jo-1 (interstitial lung disease), SAE1 cases often present with prominent soft tissue edema and severe dysphagia before characteristic rashes like Gottron's papules appear. Discuss how recognizing this serotype helps predict the severity of esophageal involvement and guides early swallowing assessments.

blogs.title: Beyond the Skin: Decoding Subcutaneous Edema in Inflammatory Myopathies
blogs.description: Challenge the misconception that angioedema is always allergic or hereditary. This educational piece dissects the pathophysiology of 'pseudo-angioedema' in dermatomyositis—caused by inflammatory muscle infiltration and fluid shifts rather than mast cell degranulation. We compare this with true angioedema mechanisms to explain why antihistamines and C1-inhibitor replacement failed in this case, reinforcing the need for a myositis workup in refractory edema.

blogs.title: The Silent Airway: Managing Severe Pharyngeal Dysphagia in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Focus on the life-threatening complication of aspiration and airway compromise seen in this case. Analyze how proximal muscle weakness leads to silent aspiration (evidenced here by post-swallow penetration despite intact anatomy on nasendoscopy). The post reviews the urgency of securing nutrition via NG tubes, monitoring respiratory status, and initiating aggressive immunomodulation (high-dose steroids + IVIG/Rituximab) to prevent fatal respiratory failure from bulbar muscle paralysis.
